title: CCS LTC • Batch 1
subtitle: Rules 1–3 · Applicability, special service conditions & scope

cards.title: The legal name
cards.rule: These rules may be called the Central Civil Services (Leave Travel Concession) Rules, 1988.
cards.explanation: Naam mein LTC ka matlab Leave Travel Concession hai. Yeh pension rules, TA on tour, ya income-tax LTA exemption ka substitute nahi hai. Pehle governing scheme identify karo, phir entitlement decide karo.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Asha submits an LTC application for a family visit. The dealing assistant opens the CCS (LTC) Rules, 1988—not the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021—to determine travel-concession eligibility.
cards.trap: A familiar acronym does not make two different schemes interchangeable.

cards.title: Commencement: publication, not signature
cards.rule: The rules come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
cards.explanation: Rule khud commencement ko Gazette publication se jodta hai. Attached master 03 May 1988 ko notification aur 21 May 1988 ko publication batata hai, lekin original Gazette issue is review mein inspect nahi hua. Isliye exact calendar date ko verified fact ki tarah memorise mat karo; publication-date test verified hai.
cards.example: Hypothetical: If a notification is signed on 3 May but published on 21 May, a publication-trigger clause takes effect on 21 May. These dates illustrate the legal test; they do not independently authenticate the actual 1988 Gazette date.
cards.trap: The exact 1988 publication day remains an open verification item.

cards.title: Included does not mean automatically entitled
cards.rule: The four covered categories are expressly subject to Rule 1(4).
cards.explanation: Pehle Rule 1(3) ka inclusion gate, phir Rule 1(4) ka exclusion gate lagao. Covered category mein aana sirf starting point hai. Service, family, leave, block, mode, fare aur claim conditions baad mein bhi apply hoti hain.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A person holds a Union civil post but works only part-time. The inclusion description alone cannot overcome the express non-whole-time exclusion in Rule 1(4)(a).
cards.trap: Do not read Rule 1(3) without its opening qualification.

cards.title: Union civil services and posts
cards.rule: Persons appointed to civil services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union are included; civilian Government servants in Defence Services are expressly included.
cards.explanation: Union ke civil services/posts coverage mein hain. Defence establishment mein kaam karna aur Armed Forces ka member hona alag legal statuses hain. Civilian employee ko sirf Defence office mein posted hone ki wajah se exclude nahi kar sakte.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Meera is a civilian Government clerk in a Defence establishment. She falls within the express civilian inclusion, subject to the remaining LTC conditions. An Army officer is tested under the Armed Forces exclusion instead.
cards.trap: Defence civilian ≠ uniformed Armed Forces member.

cards.title: State employee deputed to the Centre
cards.rule: A person employed under a State Government and on deputation with the Central Government is included.
cards.explanation: State payroll ya parent cadre dekhkar turant reject mat karo. Central Government ke saath actual deputation coverage ka basis hai. Rule 2(1) ka service-plus-certificate test bhi separately apply hota hai.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Raghav, a State Government officer, joins a Central Ministry on deputation. His parent State employment does not itself exclude him; the office must next examine his Central service and the Rule 2 certification.
cards.trap: A State employee who remains in the State post is not brought into CCS LTC merely by this clause.

cards.title: Contract appointments are included
cards.rule: Persons appointed on contract basis are a covered category.
cards.explanation: Contract par appointment ko casual labour ya outsourced agency deployment ke barabar mat samjho. Government appointment on contract identify karo; then Rule 2(1), Rule 2(2), appointment terms aur exclusions check karo. Har consultant/vendor worker ke liye automatic statutory entitlement assume nahi karna.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Neha has a direct Government appointment on a continuous three-year contract. She is not excluded merely because the appointment is contractual. A vendor-employed help-desk worker cannot establish the same coverage simply by working inside the Ministry.
cards.trap: The source analogy implying that only permanent/regular staff get LTC is misleading.

cards.title: Re-employed after retirement
cards.rule: Persons re-employed after their retirement are included.
cards.explanation: Retirement ke baad re-employment ko pensioner ki private holiday ke saath confuse mat karo. Actual re-employment appointment chahiye. Rule 2(3) gives a special continuity rule only for immediate re-employment without a break.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Dev retires and receives a Government re-employment appointment. His case enters the re-employed category; the office must examine continuity and the existing LTC account before sanction. Mere receipt of pension would not establish re-employment.
cards.trap: Coverage after re-employment is not a general LTC benefit for all retirees.

cards.title: Non-whole-time employment
cards.rule: Government servants not in whole-time employment are excluded.
cards.explanation: Yahan test whole-time employment ka hai—not simply permanent versus temporary. Temporary whole-time appointment ko part-time samajhna galat hai. Appointment record se actual status establish karo.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An official is appointed for three hours a day in a non-whole-time role. This exclusion applies even if the appointment lasts several years.
cards.trap: Long duration does not convert non-whole-time employment into whole-time employment.

cards.title: Casual and daily-rated employment
cards.rule: Persons in casual and daily-rated employment are excluded.
cards.explanation: Casual/daily-rated employment ek specific exclusion hai. Isko direct contractual appointment ki inclusion ke saath mix mat karo. Employment category documents se decide hogi; daily attendance sheet se alone legal category infer nahi karni.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Salim is engaged as a daily-rated worker. Completing twelve months of engagement alone does not remove the express exclusion.
cards.trap: One year of service is not a universal cure for an excluded category.

cards.title: Persons paid from contingencies
cards.rule: Persons paid from contingencies are excluded.
cards.explanation: Rule ka specific phrase preserve karo: persons paid from contingencies. Office ke har incidental expense ko contingency bolne se staff category establish nahi hoti. Actual engagement/payment classification verify karo.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Kavita is specifically engaged as a person paid from contingencies. Her case is excluded under clause (c); a general statement that her office has a contingency budget would not by itself prove the same status for every employee.
cards.trap: Use the actual employment/payment classification—not an invented rationale about permanence.

cards.title: Railway servants: exclusion with a limited window
cards.rule: Railway servants are generally excluded. The 2025 DoPT consolidation expressly notes conditional All India LTC once in a four-year block.
cards.explanation: Do layers alag rakho: base rule excludes; later instructions give a limited conditional All India facility. Isko full ordinary Hometown-plus-All-India entitlement mat banao. Pass-surrender mechanics require the 27 March 2018 DoPT OM and Railway implementing orders; complete current mechanics are reserved for the later audit batch.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A Railway employee asks for ordinary Hometown LTC merely because a colleague received All India LTC. That reasoning fails: the limited All India window does not itself create Hometown LTC.
cards.trap: The attached chapter 73 says one spouse’s pass surrender suffices. Conflicting Railway material indicates both spouses’ Privilege Pass surrender; do not rely on the attached statement pending primary-order reconciliation.

cards.title: Members of the Armed Forces
cards.rule: Members of the Armed Forces are excluded.
cards.explanation: Yeh exclusion service status ke liye hai. Civilian Defence employees ko yahan include karke reject karna Rule 1(3)(i) ke express inclusion ko ignore karega. Armed Forces ki apni applicable travel scheme separately dekhni hogi.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An Army officer requests a claim under these CCS LTC Rules. Membership of the Armed Forces places the officer within this exclusion; the officer’s own service travel scheme must be examined instead.
cards.trap: This says nothing about whether an Armed Forces member has benefits under a different scheme.

cards.title: Local recruits in Indian Missions abroad
cards.rule: Local recruits in Indian Missions abroad are excluded.
cards.explanation: Local recruitment abroad specific category hai. India-based staff posted to a Mission abroad ko automatically local recruit mat bolo. Unke home-leave and Mission cases later admissibility batch mein separately examine honge.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A Mission in Paris locally recruits an employee there. Clause (f) applies. An India-based officer transferred to that Mission is not excluded merely because both people work in the same building.
cards.trap: Place of work alone does not determine local-recruit status.

cards.title: Eligibility for another travel concession
cards.rule: Persons eligible to any other form of travel concession available during leave or otherwise are excluded, subject to applicable later instructions.
cards.explanation: Wording eligible hai—not only actually claimed. But har private-sector benefit, spouse arrangement, ya unrelated reimbursement ko bina specific instruction padhe automatic bar mat banao. The July 2025 FAQ expressly allows a private-sector spouse to avail the employer’s LTA/travel reimbursement. Particular overlap cases need their own instructions.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An employee says, “I was eligible for another applicable leave-travel concession but did not use it, so clause (g) cannot apply.” Non-use alone does not answer the eligibility wording; the office must check the relevant scheme and any later exception.
cards.trap: Do not turn this clause into an unsupported blanket prohibition on every employed spouse’s private LTA.

cards.title: Who faces the special service test?
cards.rule: Rule 2(1) addresses Rule 1(3)(ii), (iii) and (iv): State deputationists, contract appointees and re-employed persons.
cards.explanation: Teen categories ko distinctly identify karo. Regular civil-post category (i) ke one-year requirement ka direct reference Rule 7(1) hai. Re-employed persons ke liye Rule 2(3) ki continuity ko bhi saath read karna hoga; har re-employed person ki clock zero se restart mat karo.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A dealing assistant prepares a checklist for a State deputationist, a contract officer and an immediately re-employed officer. Rule 2 is relevant to all three, but the last case also requires the special continuity analysis.
cards.trap: Do not impose Rule 2’s special certificate on every regular employee as a universal condition.

cards.title: One year of continuous Central service
cards.rule: For the specified categories LTC is admissible on completion of one year’s continuous service under the Central Government, with the required administrative certification.
cards.explanation: Completed continuous service ek separate gate hai. Four-year contract sign karne ka matlab first day se LTC nahi. Conversely, sirf one-year completion certificate ke bina special-category case complete nahi hota. Continuity questions must be resolved from actual service records and governing orders.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Neha joins on 1 January 2026 on a four-year Government contract. For a journey on 1 July 2026, the four-year contract does not make six months into one completed year. Assume no earlier countable continuity.
cards.trap: Expected duration and completed continuous service are different tests.

cards.title: The proper administrative authority must certify
cards.rule: The appropriate administrative authority must certify the required likelihood of continued Central Government service.
cards.explanation: Employee ka personal promise aur authority ka certificate same nahi hain. Certificate record-backed hona chahiye: appointment/deputation/re-employment terms aur extension orders check karo. The rule does not name one universal designation such as DDO for every organisation.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A contract officer writes “I expect to stay four years” on an application. The office still needs certification by the appropriate administrative authority; the self-declaration alone is insufficient.
cards.trap: Do not invent a universal certifying-officer rank absent the governing provision.

cards.title: Two years, reckoned from joining
cards.rule: For Hometown LTC, certified likely Central Government service must be at least two years, reckoned from joining the Central Government post.
cards.explanation: MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION: “joining se at least 2 years” ko “journey ke baad 2 years aur bache hon” mat padho. One-year completion plus total joining-based duration test lagta hai. Actual continued service and remaining claim conditions still matter.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A direct contract runs continuously from 1 January 2026 through 31 December 2027. On 1 February 2027, one year is complete and the certified total tenure from joining is two years, although fewer than two years remain. This limb can be satisfied; the remaining LTC conditions must still be checked.
cards.trap: The uploaded master repeatedly calls this two years of future/remaining service. That is not the rule’s joining-based reckoning.

cards.ref: Rule 2(1): Any Place in India limb
cards.title: Four years, also reckoned from joining
cards.rule: For Any Place in India LTC, the certified likely service period is at least four years, reckoned from joining the Central Government post.
cards.explanation: Same anchor, higher duration. “Four additional years after application” is not the stated test. Three-year total tenure can meet the two-year Hometown duration limb but not the four-year Any Place in India limb. Certification does not create an extra block occasion.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A contract starts on 1 January 2026 and runs through 31 December 2029. On 1 February 2027, one year is complete and total certified tenure from joining is four years. Fewer than four years remain, but that alone does not defeat this duration limb.
cards.trap: Do not count four years afresh from the journey date.

cards.title: A one-year contract later extended
cards.rule: Where an initial one-year contract is later extended, the total duration of the contract is taken into account for LTC.
cards.explanation: Actual extension order important hai. One-year original contract ko permanently freeze mat karo; continuous extension ke baad total tenure evaluate karo. Rule 2(2) does not erase the one-year completed-service gate or authorize counting a break as continuous without another basis.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An initial contract covers 1 January–31 December 2026. It is continuously extended through 31 December 2029. For a February 2027 proposal, evaluate total four-year tenure from initial joining, not the initial one-year letter alone.
cards.trap: An expectation of extension is not the same as an issued extension order.

cards.title: Immediate re-employment without a break
cards.rule: For persons re-employed immediately after retirement without any break, re-employed service is treated as continuous with previous service for LTC purposes.
cards.explanation: Dono words protect karo: immediately and without any break. Is clause ka limited purpose LTC continuity hai. It does not by itself merge service for every pension/pay purpose, and it cannot be applied automatically to delayed re-employment.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An officer retires at the end of 31 October 2026 and is re-employed effective 1 November 2026 with no break. The office examines LTC continuity with prior service rather than automatically demanding a fresh year from zero.
cards.trap: If re-employment begins after a gap, this particular no-break deeming rule cannot simply be assumed.

cards.title: The “had not retired” counterfactual
cards.rule: The concession is allowed for the re-employed period provided it would have been admissible had the officer not retired but continued as a serving officer.
cards.explanation: Simple test: retire na hote to yeh LTC milti? Agar block ka occasion already used hai, continuity usko refill nahi karti. Agar entitlement unused hai, continuity can preserve its examination, but sanction still depends on the other applicable conditions.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Sana has already exhausted the relevant All India LTC occasion before retirement. Her next-day re-employment does not supply a fresh occasion in that same four-year block, because continued service without retirement would not have supplied one.
cards.trap: Continuity preserves an account; it does not reset the balance.

cards.title: Already-used All India LTC is not reborn
cards.rule: The official illustration says an officer who used Any Place in India LTC for a four-year block before retirement cannot avail it again in that block following no-break re-employment.
cards.explanation: Illustration independent new benefit nahi deta; proviso ko concrete banata hai. Calendar-year change aur fresh appointment letter ko block reset mat samjho. Next entitlement requires the applicable block and all other conditions.
cards.example: Hypothetical adaptation of the official illustration: Dev uses the 2026–2029 All India occasion in August 2026, retires on 31 October and is re-employed on 1 November. He cannot claim another 2026–2029 All India occasion merely because of re-employment.
cards.trap: The example does not establish that every possible Hometown entitlement is exhausted as well.

cards.title: Scope includes the Government servant
cards.rule: LTC covers the Government servant himself or herself and the family.
cards.explanation: Rule 3 beneficiaries ki boundary batata hai. It does not prescribe amounts, classes or frequency. Self-only travel ko sirf isliye reject nahi karna ki family saath nahi hai. Other provisions determine whether that specific journey is admissible.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An otherwise eligible employee proposes a self-only Hometown journey while the family stays home. Rule 3 does not require a family group to accompany the employee.
cards.trap: Coverage is not a promise that every expense on the holiday is reimbursable.

cards.title: “Family” is a legal definition, not a guest list
cards.rule: Family coverage must be read with the definition and conditions in Rule 4 and applicable instructions.
cards.explanation: Everyday language mein jo family/friend ho, LTC mein automatically eligible nahi. Relation, dependency aur residence tests category-wise apply hote hain; spouse exceptions bhi hain. Full Rule 4, explanations and FAQs next batch mein atomic cards par honge.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An eligible employee buys tickets for a spouse and a friend. The spouse is examined under Rule 4; friendship alone does not make the friend an LTC family beneficiary.
cards.trap: Do not copy the pension/medical-benefit definition of family into LTC.

cards.title: Family need not always travel with the employee
cards.rule: The July 2025 FAQ permits the employee and eligible family members to travel separately or in groups at different times and, where applicable, to different destinations within the relevant block.
cards.explanation: Rule 3 ko “sab ek saath hi jaayenge” mat padho. Family-only travel employee se derived entitlement hai, but separate journeys allowed hain. Detailed leave, block-debit, fare anchor and return-time mechanics later batches mein covered honge.
cards.example: Hypothetical: An eligible employee takes an admissible journey in June; eligible family members propose travel in October against the relevant entitlement. Separate dates alone do not disqualify the family proposal. All person-wise block and travel conditions still need checking.
cards.trap: Separate travel does not create a duplicate occasion for the same person.

cards.title: Autonomous-body officers deputed to the Centre
cards.rule: Officers of autonomous bodies deputed to the Central Government are treated as temporary Government servants during that deputation and allowed LTC accordingly.
cards.explanation: Is note se deputation-period treatment established hai. Parent body mein serving every employee ko automatic CCS entitlement nahi milta. Also, note itself does not expressly put every such officer into Rule 1(3)(ii): that clause specifically says State Government. Do not infer every Rule 2 certificate solely from the word temporary; verify the officer’s category and deputation terms.
cards.example: Hypothetical: Iqbal, an autonomous-body officer, is deputed to a Central Ministry. His case cannot be rejected only because his parent employer is autonomous. The office applies the temporary-Government-servant treatment for the deputation period and checks the applicable service conditions.
cards.trap: The uploaded guide automatically infers the Rule 2 certificate from temporary status. That inference is not expressly stated in this note.

cards.title: Industrial/work-charged staff with regular leave
cards.rule: Industrial and work-charged staff entitled to regular leave are eligible for LTC like other Central Government employees; the note records their first block as 1960–61.
cards.explanation: Job label se blanket exclusion nahi. Regular-leave entitlement yahan expressly important hai. This positive note does not cancel Rule 1(4)’s exclusions; where classifications overlap, examine the actual appointment record and governing instructions. The 1960–61 figure is historical, not today’s usable block.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A work-charged employee entitled to regular leave is told that all work-charged staff are excluded. The note contradicts that blanket answer. The office should examine the actual appointment and remaining LTC conditions.
cards.trap: Do not use the historical 1960–61 starting block as a current travel occasion.

cards.title: The consolidation’s own disclaimer
cards.rule: The consolidation says that in a contradiction or imprecision the relevant OMs/orders prevail and the discrepancy may be brought to DoPT’s notice.
cards.explanation: Consolidated document useful official reference hai, but every summary ko amendment mat bolo. Specific instrument, date, scope and legal validity check karo. Later departmental implementation does not automatically amend statutory rules for everybody. Relevant current instruments must also be read consistently with the statutory rules.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A consolidated paragraph contains an unclear time period, but the applicable specific OM states the condition clearly. The office records the OM reference and resolves the discrepancy instead of treating a convenient summary as a new rule.
cards.trap: Age alone does not make an instruction obsolete; supersession, amendment, scope and expiry matter.

cards.title: Apply the gates in order
cards.rule: Identify category → apply exclusion/exception → test special service conditions → preserve prior entitlement history → identify self/eligible family → check remaining journey rules.
cards.explanation: Yeh teaching checklist hai, naya rule nahi. Batch 1 sirf coverage aur special service conditions complete karta hai. Family detail, leave, block, entitlement, booking aur claim sanction baaki batches mein independently verify honge.
cards.example: Hypothetical: A direct contract officer has completed one year, has an extended four-year tenure certified from initial joining and requests travel with a spouse. Batch 1 may establish the initial service gates. The office must still verify Rule 4 family status, leave, block occasion, route, mode, fare and claim compliance before payment.
cards.trap: Passing Batch 1’s gates is not a final sanction decision.

quiz.q: A Defence civilian clerk and an Armed Forces officer work at the same establishment. Are both excluded?
quiz.a: No. Civilian Defence Government servants are expressly included under Rule 1(3)(i); Armed Forces members are excluded under Rule 1(4)(e), subject to their separate schemes.

quiz.q: A contract officer has a certified four-year tenure from joining but only six months of completed service. Does duration alone satisfy Rule 2?
quiz.a: No. The completed one-year continuous-service gate is separate; assume no earlier countable continuity.

quiz.q: After one year is complete, must a two-year contract officer still have two years remaining for Hometown LTC?
quiz.a: No. The two-year certified duration is reckoned from joining the Central Government post, not afresh from the journey date. Other conditions still apply.

quiz.q: A one-year initial contract is continuously extended to four years. Is the original one-year duration frozen?
quiz.a: No. Rule 2(2) takes total extended contract duration into account.

quiz.q: No-break re-employment follows an already-used All India LTC. Does a fresh appointment letter refill the same block?
quiz.a: No. Rule 2(3), its proviso and official illustration preserve continuity but do not duplicate the exhausted occasion.

quiz.q: Must every autonomous-body deputationist obtain the Rule 2 certificate merely because the note says temporary Government servant?
quiz.a: Do not infer that solely from the note. Verify the actual appointment category, applicable service conditions and deputation terms; the note itself grants temporary-servant treatment during deputation.

quiz.q: Does a conditional Railway All India facility establish ordinary Hometown LTC?
quiz.a: No. The official consolidation acknowledges a limited conditional All India window, not full ordinary coverage.

quiz.q: Is an exact 21 May 1988 commencement day officially authenticated in this batch?
quiz.a: No. The publication-date trigger is checked; the original Gazette issue and exact publication day remain pending.

voices.style: City Hinglish: everyday conversational Hindi + English; English legal terms, dates and numbers; no formal or difficult Hindi. Condensed audio, not a verbatim legal reading.

audio_revision: Clause-reference edition: all 30 written cards mapped once, in order, to a spoken reference, explanation and hypothetical example. Rule 2(1) has unlettered conditions, not invented lettered clauses. Supplementary guideline notes, FAQ cross-references and the teaching checklist are labelled separately. Same selected city-Hinglish voices. Existing evidence limits retained.
